notes_list.title: Oxidizing Agents — KMnO4 and Cr(VI)
notes_list.basic_overview: Common oxidants differ in strength, selectivity and medium. Permanganate is versatile; Cr(VI) reagents can oxidize alcohols and carbonyl precursors depending on water content and formulation.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Primary alcohols can stop at aldehydes under controlled anhydrous conditions or proceed to acids under aqueous strong oxidation. Secondary alcohols give ketones. Alkenes can undergo oxidation/cleavage under stronger conditions.
notes_list.examples: KMnO4: alcohol oxidation, alkene dihydroxylation/cleavage depending conditions. PCC: primary alcohol → aldehyde. Jones reagent: primary alcohol → acid in aqueous acidic medium.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Acidic/basic medium and temperature dramatically change permanganate behavior. PCC is commonly used under relatively anhydrous conditions.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Oxidation often proceeds through formation of a metal-bound alkoxide/chromate ester followed by hydride transfer for alcohol oxidation. Alkene permanganate chemistry can proceed through cyclic intermediates.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Reaction rate depends on oxidant concentration, substrate, medium and temperature; mechanistic pathways differ by oxidant.
notes_list.common_traps: Never choose an oxidant by name alone; identify substrate and desired stopping point.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
